text:
sam: Heads-up — since ~08:10 UTC eu-west1 saw a sharp spike in outbound egress; lots of controller-manager restarts and a handful of apiserver 5xxs. GPU onboarding stuck in 'attaching'. I think conntrack exhaustion or SNAT client ports.
andre: I see the same in grafana: NAT bytes up, conntrack entries hitting ~95% on several nodes. apiserver logs show TCP reset from kubelet health probes.
kate: @oncall-sre can you grab node conntrack and kube-proxy logs? Any recent egress changes rolled out?
deploy-bot: Deployed rollout "egress-nat-rewrite" to eu-west1 at 08:05 UTC by kate — status: success
maria: Running quick checks: `sudo conntrack -S` -> entries: 429400 on node-az1 (limit 524288). Many CLOSE_WAIT/TIME_WAIT for kubelet->apiserver streams.
paul: Suggestion: temporarily throttle gpu-provisioner onboarding, switch provisioner to managed egress IPs (to reduce SNAT fanout), and scale controller-manager to 3 replicas to spread load.
sam: I can throttle the provisioner. There's an internal API to set claim rate: `curl -X POST https://internal-api/provisioner/scale -d '{"rate":0.2}'` — can run if approved.
kate: approved. pausing new gpu claims for 10m. Also I'm rolling back egress-nat-rewrite in eu-west1 now.
andre: After the rollback, conntrack entries started to decline and apiserver 5xxs dropped ~50% within 3 minutes. nvme snapshot IOPS still a bit high on two controlplane nodes, watching.
maria: Quick follow-ups: add a soft limit in provisioner to avoid onboarding bursts, add exponential backoff for node attach retries, and document a runbook. Filed INC-12345 with initial timeline and raw metrics link: https://grafana.redwood/d/xyz
paul: Good. Let's run a short postmortem and include network team for the egress rule audit. cc @security.
sam: thanks all — monitoring closely, will update if anything changes. :thumbsup:
